6 euclid_intro_sentence "2.8.0"
7 "If a straight-line is cut at random, (then) four times the rectangle contained by the whole (straight-line), and one of the pieces (of the straight-line), plus the square on the remaining piece, is equal to the square described on the whole and the former piece, as on one (complete straight-line). For let any straight-line $AB$ be cut, at random, at point $C$. I say that four times the rectangle contained by $AB$ and $BC$, plus the square on $AC$, is equal to the square described on $AB$ and $BC$, as on one (complete straight-line)."
